headline: Colombian forces free 76 hostages in Cartagena supermarket
pages: Colombian security forces freed about 76 shoppers and employees held hostage for roughly 17 hours at a supermarket in Cartagena. Gunmen entered the store at 8 a.m. Tuesday after a failed attempt to rob an armored car carrying money. They held people at gunpoint while trying to negotiate an escape. The assailants released 10 hostages earlier, including elderly women. As the standoff dragged on, President Abelardo de la Espriella approved a raid by special forces and police. Officers used stun grenades, and nearby residents heard explosions. One gunman was killed and four were arrested.

De la Espriella flew to Cartagena to oversee the operation and called it an extraordinary joint effort carried out flawlessly. He said the gunmen had been offered the chance to surrender and refused. Source: BBC News.
